citations.source: 李学勤主编，《字源》，天津古籍出版社、辽宁人民出版社，2012; directly inspected original scan, PDF p. 71, printed p. 59, with bounded headword and continuation crops.
citations.field: Lower-left 荼 entry: headword, reading, phonetic component, proposed original meaning; same-page continuation at top of right column
citations.text: The headword is 荼, read tú; its printed lower portion shows two horizontal bars below the roof-like strokes, crossing the central vertical. The entry calls 荼 a phono-semantic character formed from 艸 with 余 as phonetic and proposes 苦菜 (bitter edible plant) as its original meaning. It cites 《说文》 “荼，苦荼也” and 《尔雅·释草》 “荼，苦菜.” The paragraph continues at the top of the facing right column on this same page: it says the bitter taste of this plant could be compared to hardship and quotes 《书·汤诰》 “弗忍荼毒.” These are the book’s attributed claims about 荼, not 茶. They do not establish that the bitter-plant sense is the source of the tea sense, nor identify the plant in every historical occurrence of 荼.
